document.title: IIR [Excised]/Veteran Afghanistan Traveler's Analysis of Al Qaeda and Taliban Military, Political and Cultural Landscape and its Weaknesses
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Secret] Details events in Afghanistan and Pakistan's role in supporting the Taliban. Pakistan groomed weak commanders like Hekmatyar, whose failure led it to introduce the Taliban. Notes Musharraf's troubling position hunting culprits he helped establish, and summarizes al-Qaeda and Pakistani agendas and the death of Masoud.

persons.name: Gulbadin Hekmatyar
persons.role: Afghan mujahideen party leader favored by Pakistan; principal beneficiary of Pakistani policy

mentions.quote: THE PRINCIPAL BENEFICIARY OF THIS POLICY WAS GULBADIN ((HEKMATYR)).
HEKMATYR WAS INCOMPETENT. HE WAS NEVER ABLE TO WREST KABUL FROM MASSOUD

persons.name: Ahmad Shah Massoud
persons.role: Tajik commander from northern Afghanistan; United Front leader, captured Kabul; chief rival of Taliban
persons.status_detail: murdered; death described as serving both Taliban and al-Qaeda (Sept 2001)

mentions.quote: IT WAS AHMAD SHAH ((MASSOUD)) WHO CAPTURED IT, NOT HEKMATYR
MASSOUD'S DEATH SERVED BOTH TALIBAN AND AL QAEDA.

persons.name: Jalaluddin Haqqani
persons.role: Local Afghan mujahideen commander and influential tribal leader from Paktia; hosted Arabs at Zhawar facility

mentions.quote: THE LOCAL AFGHAN MUJAHIDEEN COMMANDER WAS JALALUDIN ((HAQANI)).
THE ISI PRESSURED HAQANI TO UNDERTAKE ACTION AGAINST MATUN
FOR THE TALIBAN PAKISTAN CHOSE MULLAH MOHAMMAD ((OMAR)), WHO WAS WILLING TO DO AS HE WAS TOLD.
THE BIN LADEN BRAND OF EXTREMISM HAS BEEN ABLE TO GROW UNMOLESTED INSIDE AFGHANISTAN.
DEMANDS TO DELIVER BIN LADEN MAY HAVE ALREADY BROUGHT ABOUT THE REALIZATION

persons.name: Pervez Musharraf
persons.role: Pakistani president/general asked to help hunt al-Qaeda

mentions.quote: DEEPLY TROUBLING PERIOD FOR GENERAL ((MUSHARRAF)) IN PAKISTAN, WHO IS ASKED TO HELP HUNT DOWN THE CULPRITS

persons.name: Mohammad Fahim
persons.role: New commander of Massoud's United Front

mentions.quote: GENERAL MOHAMMAD ((FAHIM)) IS RECORDED AS THE NEW COMMANDER OF MASSOUD'S UNITED FRONT.

events.description: Soviet withdrawal followed by civil war; ISI-directed attacks on Jalalabad.
Ahmad Shah Massoud murdered; Fahim succeeded him.
DIA information report issued on al-Qaeda and Taliban weaknesses.
Murder of Ahmad Shah Massoud, described as serving both Taliban and al-Qa'ida; Mohammad Fahim recorded as new United Front commander.
General Mohammad Fahim recorded as new commander of the United Front.
Soviet withdrawal; civil war began between Afghan communist government remnants and mujahideen groups, with ISI-directed attacks on Jalalabad.
Special facility for Arab volunteers constructed at Zhawar, Paktia, with ISI funding.
Kabul fell and was captured by Massoud; Pakistan then backed Hekmatyar in another civil war.
Pakistan abandoned Hekmatyar and created the Taliban under Mullah Omar.
ISI pressured Haqqani to attack Matun in Khost.
DIA information report on veteran traveler's analysis of al-Qa'ida and Taliban landscape.
Fall of Kabul, captured by Massoud rather than Pakistan-favored Hekmatyar, leading to renewed civil war.
After the Soviet withdrawal, ISI-directed conventional assaults on Jalalabad by mujahideen failed with heavy casualties.
ISI pressured Haqqani to act against Matun; Taliban emerged with Pakistani backing under Omar.
Death of Ahmad Shah Massoud, which served both the Taliban and al-Qaeda.

relationships.detail: Haqqani belonged to the Jadran tribe and negotiated land use.
relationships.quote: HAQANI WAS ABLE TO NEGOTIATE THE USE OF THE LAND FROM THE JADRAN TRIBE HE BELONGED TO.

relationships.quote: THE ARAB VISITORS WERE LARGELY LINKED AND RELIANT ON HAQANI'S MUJAHIDEEN IN PAKTIA.

relationships.detail: ISI pressured Haqqani to act against Matun/Khost.
relationships.quote: THE ISI PRESSURED HAQANI TO UNDERTAKE ACTION AGAINST MATUN

relationships.detail: Pakistan chose Omar for the Taliban and ISI is credited with his emergence.
relationships.quote: OMAR'S EMERGENCE IS CREDITED TO PAKISTAN ISI ACTIONS.

relationships.detail: Omar led the Taliban.
relationships.quote: FOR THE TALIBAN PAKISTAN CHOSE MULLAH MOHAMMAD ((OMAR))

relationships.detail: Pakistan groomed and backed Hekmatyar with logistics and manpower.
relationships.quote: DESPITE MASSIVE LOGISTICAL AND MATERIAL (INCLUDING MANPOWER) SUPPORT FROM PAKISTAN.

relationships.detail: Hekmatyar never wrested Kabul from Massoud.
relationships.quote: HE WAS NEVER ABLE TO WREST KABUL FROM MASSOUD

relationships.detail: Fahim recorded as new commander of Massoud's United Front.
relationships.quote: GENERAL MOHAMMAD ((FAHIM)) IS RECORDED AS THE NEW COMMANDER OF MASSOUD'S UNITED FRONT.

relationships.detail: Taliban fully supported by Pakistan.
relationships.quote: THE FULLY SUPPORTED (BY PAKISTAN) TALIBAN PREVAILS

relationships.detail: Taliban at war with United Front.
relationships.quote: THE WAR BETWEEN UNITED FRONT AND TALIBAN IS NOT A WAR ABOUT INTERPRETATIONS OF ISLAM.

relationships.detail: Bin Laden's extremism grew unmolested under the Taliban umbrella.
relationships.quote: UNDER THE SHADE OF THE TALIBAN UMBRELLA THE BIN LADEN BRAND OF EXTREMISM HAS BEEN ABLE TO GROW

relationships.detail: 055 Brigade members serve with Taliban forces but are not integrated.
relationships.quote: MEMBERS OF 055 BRIGADE MIGHT SERVE WITH TALIBAN FORCES, BUT THEY ARE NOT IN ANY WESTERN SENSE INTEGRATED.

relationships.detail: The Taliban remain heavily reliant on Pakistan support, though Pakistan struggles to keep control over them.
relationships.quote: WHILE STILL HEAVILY RELIANT ON PAKISTAN SUPPORT, THE TALIBAN HAS NOW REMAINED IN POWER LONG ENOUGH TO DEVELOP AN INDEPENDENT MOMENTUM

relationships.detail: Pakistan created, imposed and recognized the Taliban, which proved unpredictable and ungrateful.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN CREATED, IMPOSED AND RECOGNIZED BY PAKISTAN PROVED UNPREDICTABLE AND UNGRATEFUL.

relationships.detail: The Taliban accepted fundamentalist non-Afghans in their fighting force and rely on al-Qa'ida support, though agendas differ.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN HAD LITTLE TIME TO THINK THROUGH WHAT THE PRICE OF AL QAEDA SUPPORT MIGHT MEAN IN THE LONG TERM.

relationships.detail: Al-Qa'ida's agenda differs from the Taliban's; long term there is no room for Taliban in its ambitions.
relationships.quote: LONG TERM THERE CAN BE NO ROOM FOR TALIBAN IN THEIR AMBITIONS.

relationships.detail: 055 Brigade members may serve with Taliban forces but are not integrated, remaining like an international brigade.
relationships.quote: MEMBERS OF 055 BRIGADE MIGHT SERVE WITH TALIBAN FORCES, BUT THEY ARE NOT IN ANY WESTERN SENSE INTEGRATED.

relationships.detail: The text discusses 055 Brigade in the context of the al-Qa'ida agenda as a distinct non-Afghan force.
relationships.quote: THEY REMAIN RATHER LIKE AN INTERNATIONAL BRIGADE, DIFFERENT IN LANGUAGE, HABIT AND IN THE INTERPRETATION OF ISLAM.

relationships.detail: Musharraf is asked to help hunt down culprits Pakistan helped establish and support.
relationships.quote: GENERAL MUSHARRAF IN PAKISTAN, WHO IS ASKED TO HELP HUNT DOWN THE CULPRITS THAT HE HELPED TO ESTABLISH AND SUPPORTED.

relationships.detail: The Taliban focused on destroying the United Front and other opposition factions.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN WAS FOCUSED ON THE DESTRUCTION OF THE UNITED FRONT AND OTHER OPPOSITION FACTIONS.

relationships.detail: Demands to deliver bin Laden may have led Taliban to realize they cannot demand anything of al-Qa'ida.
relationships.quote: DEMANDS TO DELIVER BIN LADEN MAY HAVE ALREADY BROUGHT ABOUT THE REALIZATION THAT THE TALIBAN IS NO LONGER IN A POSITION TO DEMAND ANYTHING OF AL QAEDA.

relationships.detail: Massoud was the chief rival of the Taliban.
relationships.quote: HE WAS THE CHIEF RIVAL OF TALIBAN AND THE CHIEF THORN IN AL QAEDA'S AMBITIONS AS WELL.

relationships.detail: Massoud was the chief thorn in al-Qa'ida's ambitions.
relationships.quote: THE CHIEF THORN IN AL QAEDA'S AMBITIONS AS WELL.

sources_cited: Veteran Afghanistan traveler (source of IIR, DOI 2001-09-24)
key_claims: Pakistan's ISI created and imposed the Taliban to secure a compliant proxy regime but has lost control of it.
Al-Qa'ida's agenda in Afghanistan differs from the Taliban's and has no long-term room for them.
Arab visitors incubating al-Qa'ida in Paktia were reliant on Haqqani's mujahideen, with a facility funded by ISI.
The Taliban rule much of Afghanistan without 90 percent popular support; exploiting Taliban–al-Qaeda differences is advised.
Massoud's murder served both Taliban and al-Qaeda.
Selective humanitarian aid beyond Taliban control is recommended to help eradicate al-Qaeda.
